draft.title: Why change the Constitution
card: The Australian Constitution was drafted in the 1890s and took effect in 1901. It sets out how the Commonwealth Parliament, the executive and the courts work.
Australian society has changed a great deal since then. Values, technology and ideas about rights are not the same as they were.
Because of this, changes may be sought to reflect new values, to recognise or protect rights, or to update how Australia is governed.
A proposed change is not certain to be made. It is a request that must go through the process set out in the Constitution.
draft.remember: A document from the 1890s may not fit modern values, rights or ways of governing, so change may be sought.

a.q: Which is the best reason someone might give for seeking a change to the Constitution?
opts: It was written in the 1890s and may not match modern values
It is no longer in force because it is so old
Parliament cannot pass any laws without a change
Courts have asked for it to be rewritten every decade
a.why: A document from the 1890s may not match current values, rights or ways of governing, so people may seek change. It is still in force today, so the claim that it no longer applies is wrong.
a.clue: Think about what has changed in society since the 1890s.

b.q: Jess argues that the Constitution should be changed to protect a right that Australians now widely value but it does not mention. Which idea does her argument rest on?
opts: Ideas about rights have changed since the 1890s
The Constitution has ceased to be law
Changes are required every few years
Only the courts can decide which rights matter
b.why: Jess is saying that the 1890s document does not reflect a right people now value, so change may be sought. Her argument does not claim the Constitution has stopped being law.
b.clue: Her argument is about a gap between an old document and today's values.

a.best: It was written in the 1890s and may not match modern values

b.best: Ideas about rights have changed since the 1890s

proposal.title: Why change the Constitution
card: The Australian Constitution was drafted in the 1890s and took effect in 1901. It is still in force, and there is no set timetable for changing it.
Australian society has changed a great deal since 1901. Changes may be sought so the document reflects what Australians now believe is fair or important.
The Constitution protects only a few rights directly, such as freedom of religion. Changes may be sought to protect rights it does not mention.
Changes may be sought to update how power is shared or how government is set up, such as recognising local councils or becoming a republic.
proposal.remember: An 1890s document may not fit today, so change may be sought to reflect new values, protect rights or update how Australia is governed.

a.q: The Constitution does not mention the Prime Minister. A group wants to add rules about the role. Which reason best fits?
opts: Updating how power is shared in government
Adding protection for a right it lacks
Reflecting new beliefs about what is fair
Meeting a set timetable for regular review
a.why: Rules about the Prime Minister's role change how government is set up and how power is shared, so this is about ways of governing. It is not a right held by people, and there is no set timetable that requires review.
a.clue: Would the change affect people's freedoms, or how government is set up?

b.q: Jess argues that the Constitution should be changed to protect a right that Australians now widely value but it does not mention. Which idea does her argument rest on?
opts: Ideas about rights have changed since the 1890s
The Constitution has ceased to be law
Changes are required every few years
The Constitution already protects most rights
b.why: Jess is saying the 1890s document leaves out a right people now value, so change may be sought to protect it. The Constitution protects only a few rights directly, so her argument does not assume it already protects most of them.
b.clue: Her argument is about a gap between an old document and what people value today.

a.best: Updating how power is shared in government

b.best: Ideas about rights have changed since the 1890s
